question: Reactions in which there is an exchange of ions, between the reactants are called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**double displacement reactions.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reactions in which there is an exchange of ions between the reactants are called **double displacement reactions** or **metathesis reactions**.
 
• 
 
The general form of the equation is shown below:

 
 AB(aq)+CD(aq) to AD(aq)+CB(aq)

 
 
• Further double displacement reactions can be classified into two types:
 
• Neutralisation reactions:
 
 
• They take place between an acid and a base.
 
• HCl(aq)+NaOH(aq) to NaCl(aq)+H₂O(l)
 
 
 
• Precipitation reactions:
 
 
• Involve the formation of the undissolved residue
 
• AgNO₃(aq)+KCl(aq) to KNO₃(aq)+AgCl(s)
 
 
 
• 
 In these reactions, the cations and anions of the reactants switch places, forming new compounds.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Exchange Reactions**

 
 
• Exchange reactions involve the exchange of parts between two compounds.
 
• This category can encompass a variety of reactions, including double displacement reactions.
 
• **Example**: A general form can be represented as:AB+CD→AD+CB
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• **​** Displacement reactions occur when one element displaces another in a compound.
 
• These reactions can be categorized into single displacement (or single replacement) and double displacement.
 
• **Example**: A single displacement reaction can be represented as:A+BC→A C + B 
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reactions ****​**
 
 
• Double displacement reactions (also known as double replacement reactions) involve two compounds exchanging their ions to form two new compounds.
 
• **Example**: A typical double displacement reaction can be represented as:A B + C D → A D + C B
